blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Addresses with a non-ASCII character are logged in full) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (Percent-encoded addresses in URLs are not masked) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: The local part and the domain only accept ASCII letters, so an internationalized address does not match at all and passes through unmasked: `logInfo("signup", { user: "josé@example.fr" })` writes `josé@example.fr` (the character before `@` is `é`, outside the class), and `ada@exämple.de` is likewise left whole. The customer's e-mail address then reaches the hosting provider's logs, kept 90 days — the very leak the proposal removes (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 25). Match any non-space, non-`@` characters around the `@` (e.g. Unicode-aware `[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]{2,}` with the `u` flag), and add a test with a non-ASCII local part and domain.
findings.title: Addresses with a non-ASCII character are logged in full

findings.recommendation: The pattern requires a literal `@`, so an address carried in a URL or query string, such as `/reset?email=ada.lovelace%40example.org`, is logged in full when a caller logs a request path or URL. No caller exists in this diff, hence the low confidence. Also match the encoded `%40` form (case-insensitive), or decode before masking, and cover it with a test.
findings.title: Percent-encoded addresses in URLs are not masked

findings.evidence:
for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(fields)) {
  safe[key] = typeof value === "string" ? maskEmails(value) : value;
findings.recommendation: Only values go through `maskEmails`; the keys are copied as they are. A caller that builds fields keyed by an address (e.g. a per-user counter `{ [email]: count }`) writes the full address to the log. It depends on callers not in this diff. Mask the keys too, or document that keys must be constant identifiers.
findings.title: Field names are written to the log without masking

findings.recommendation: `a***@example.org` is pseudonymised, not anonymous: for a customer on a personal or small-company domain, the first letter plus the domain is enough to re-identify them in the 90-day logs. Whether that matters depends on the customer base, which the review could not see. If the domain is not needed for diagnosis, mask it too (e.g. `a***@***`) or log an opaque user id instead.
findings.title: The masked form keeps the domain and first letter
